newsitem.title: FRANCE: France praises Togo's economy, political reforms.
newsitem.headline: France praises Togo's economy, political reforms.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe praised Togo's economy and political reforms on Tuesday and promised continued French support for the African nation ruled since 1967 by President Gnassingbe Eyadema.
"I have been impressed by the advance of reforms undertaken in Togo, notably on the political level," Juppe said after talks with Togo's Prime Minister Kwassi Klutse in Paris.
"Democratic institutions are being put in place. We are delighted by this in France," he told reporters of the former African nation.
"Progress has been made on the economic front. There is growth and inflation is under control," he said.
"There are obviously still difficulties, as in all countries, but Togo can count on France's support and especially its aid once things are in place with the International Monetary Fund," he said.

Klutse said he was "satisfied" with his visit "and of the support France is willing to give to support us in the vigourous actions we are carrying out." Togo's gross domestic product expanded by a strong 8.3 percent in real terms in 1995.

France broke with its European allies in 1994 by resuming aid to Togo, which has had a bumpy transition to multi-party rule. France had been the last country to cut off aid in 1993 after peace talks between Eyadema and the opposition broke down.
Eyadema, in power since 1967 when he staged independent black Africa's first coup d'etat, was elected president in 1993 in a vote boycotted by the opposition.
